latest_published_release.name: ModelDock 0.2.0 — Large-file preview and model comparison
latest_published_release.body:
ModelDock lets you open reconstruction models and CAD files directly in an editor or supported desktop host. This release adds bounded large-file previews and a shared model-comparison workflow.

## 新增功能

- 四个入口默认允许最高 8 GiB 的源文件：VS Code、DeepSeek Harness、兼容的 OpenAI Desktop 文件入口、独立本地查看器。
- 超过 5 GiB 的二进制 PLY/STL 使用有界分段读取：PLY 最多显示 30 万个采样点，STL 最多显示 10 万个采样三角面；保留原始数量、坐标原点及采样说明。
- 多模型工作流：添加模型 → 选择参考/真值 → 按需对齐 → 比较。支持多 PLY 叠加、同步分屏、透明度、局部刚性 ICP、显式平移/旋转/缩放和重置。
- 可导入 STL 网格作为参考真值，计算双向距离统计、RMSE、P95、采样最大值、Chamfer、精确率、召回率和 F-score；支持误差热图、逐个对参考评价，以及 JSON/CSV 导出。
- 自动刷新保留视角、其他模型、参考选择及变换；中英文界面。

## 安装包

发布工作流会自动附加以下文件：

| 文件 | 用途 |
| --- | --- |
| modeldock-0.2.0.vsix | VS Code：扩展菜单 → 从 VSIX 安装；也适用于在 VS Code 中使用 Codex 的工作流 |
| dsh-plugin-modeldock-0.2.0.tgz | DeepSeek Harness 原生文件预览插件 |
| modeldock-openai-0.2.0.zip | 支持文件入口及授权资源读取的 OpenAI Desktop 插件 |
| modeldock-0.2.0-source.zip | 完整源码、预构建运行文件、安装包、许可及匹配的 CAD 依赖源码 |
| SHA256SUMS.txt | 四个归档的 SHA-256 校验值 |

使用说明：[中文 README](https://github.com/Afloat16/modeldock/blob/main/README.zh-CN.md) · [Harness 安装](https://github.com/Afloat16/modeldock/blob/main/adapters/deepseek-harness/README.md) · [OpenAI Desktop 安装](https://github.com/Afloat16/modeldock/blob/main/docs/openai-integration.md)。

## 验证与边界

- 105 项自动测试；共享浏览器 15 组、对比界面 9 组、OpenAI 旧资源路径 7 组、大文件范围路径 6 组，另有真实 stdio 验证。
- 真实安装的 DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-alpha.2 Web 通过 8 组检查，包括超过 5 GiB 的 PLY/STL；真实 VS Code 1.96.4 已在 GitHub CI 中通过四阶段原生验收，包括这两种大文件。
- 大文件用例使用真实稀疏文件，验证大小、偏移、范围读取和渲染，不代表密集 5 GiB 数据的吞吐性能基准。
- 5 GiB 能力是二进制 PLY/STL 的采样预览；大型 PLY 网格当前仅显示采样顶点，面拓扑会明确标为省略。其他格式保持 128 MiB 普通解析边界；不支持完整 5 GiB STEP/IGES/BREP 转换。
- 比较指标描述加载/采样后的几何，最大值不是精确 Hausdorff 距离；单位必须确认，ICP 不自动修正比例，也不保证全局配准。
- OpenAI 使用真实应用和 MCP 服务、模拟 Desktop 宿主进行验证；尚未完成专有 Desktop 软件的实际安装验收。CLI、Work Web 和移动端不声明原生 3D 文件入口能力。
- 发布前依赖扫描为 0 项已知漏洞；这不等于独立安全审计。

详见 [验证记录](https://github.com/Afloat16/modeldock/blob/main/docs/validation.md)。原始项目源码和原创样例采用 MIT；CAD 依赖保留自身 LGPL 许可，匹配源码随完整源码包提供。

最终发布提交：`2f93e45f0b47ee7f842abd9f86ddcc4e79983c4c`。[完整 CI 已通过](https://github.com/Afloat16/modeldock/actions/runs/40856160717)，包含浏览器流程、依赖审计和独立的 VS Code 原生任务。

latest_published_release.name: v0.2.0 - Email-first workflow instructions
latest_published_release.body:
## Email-first human input

Send the complete reviewed steps and an ordinary official login/action link in the email. There is no blanket requirement to return to GPT for every interaction.

- Optional canonical `action`: bounded numbered steps, ordinary reply prompt, and completion hint
- Explicit email-only action opt-in: `AAN_INCLUDE_ACTION=1` or `--include-action` in the producer
- Configured `AAN_SMTP_REPLY_TO`, exact transmitted Message-ID, request reference and current revision
- `aan replies ingest --file message.eml` and `aan replies list` for a durable unverified-input review inbox
- Current-request checks, replay/conflict protection, bounded MIME parsing, and obsolete-note handling
- Additive SQLite v1 → v2 migration, preserving existing event identities, pending requests, and queued deliveries
- Explicit database paths work without a home-directory profile

[English setup](https://github.com/Afloat16/agent-action-notifier/blob/v0.2.0/docs/email-first.md) · [中文设置指南](https://github.com/Afloat16/agent-action-notifier/blob/v0.2.0/docs/email-first.zh-CN.md)

## Important limits

Reply import is local and explicit. This release does not poll a mailbox, authenticate an email author, create an agent-answer channel, or configure SMTP/provider access. Imported replies always remain `pending_unverified` with `can_authorize: false`; they cannot approve, execute, resolve, or resume actions. A separately authorized host must establish owner intent and apply its original confirmation policy. Required platform confirmation forms still use their required surface. Passwords and sign-in credentials stay on the official service.

Defaults remain generic. Review action content before opting in: heuristic redaction cannot guarantee removal of private information. SMTP acceptance does not prove inbox delivery or human attention. No live SMTP/inbox/desktop end-to-end delivery was established.

## Upgrading

Back up your existing SQLite state using a consistent SQLite backup while producers/workers are stopped; do not copy only a live WAL-backed `.db` file. First use of 0.2.0 upgrades the database to schema v2. Version 0.1.0 cannot open that upgraded schema; downgrade requires your retained v1 backup. Nothing installs a background service or creates credentials.

## Downloads

Python 3.10+ is required. The `.pyz` runs without third-party runtime dependencies or package installation. The wheel and source archive are alternatives. Verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

## 中文摘要

新版本可以将经审阅的完整操作步骤和官方登录/操作入口直接写进邮件，并提供普通问题的回复提示，不再要求每次都回到 GPT。需要在生产方明确启用邮件正文，并自行配置 SMTP 和回复邮箱。

本地 `.eml` 导入只生成“未经验证的待处理输入”，不会自动收邮件、确认身份、授权、执行或恢复任务。平台要求的确认表单仍须在指定界面完成；密码与登录凭据留在官方服务。升级会保留旧事件、请求和发送队列并迁移数据库，回退旧版本须使用提前保存的一致性备份。

## Verification

158 unique stdlib tests pass locally. The exact final commit `80a5cd2f881c5e7a62e03cfcf9dac2bb5780266b` passed all nine Linux/macOS/Windows × Python 3.10/3.12/3.14 CI jobs, including compilation and zipapp smoke. SMTP tests are mocked; webhook tests exercise real loopback HTTP. The zipapp, wheel, and source archive were checked byte-for-byte against committed Python source. [CI evidence](https://github.com/Afloat16/agent-action-notifier/actions/runs/37247755439).

published_releases.body:
ModelDock lets you open reconstruction models and CAD files directly in an editor or supported desktop host. This release adds bounded large-file previews and a shared model-comparison workflow.

## 新增功能

- 四个入口默认允许最高 8 GiB 的源文件：VS Code、DeepSeek Harness、兼容的 OpenAI Desktop 文件入口、独立本地查看器。
- 超过 5 GiB 的二进制 PLY/STL 使用有界分段读取：PLY 最多显示 30 万个采样点，STL 最多显示 10 万个采样三角面；保留原始数量、坐标原点及采样说明。
- 多模型工作流：添加模型 → 选择参考/真值 → 按需对齐 → 比较。支持多 PLY 叠加、同步分屏、透明度、局部刚性 ICP、显式平移/旋转/缩放和重置。
- 可导入 STL 网格作为参考真值，计算双向距离统计、RMSE、P95、采样最大值、Chamfer、精确率、召回率和 F-score；支持误差热图、逐个对参考评价，以及 JSON/CSV 导出。
- 自动刷新保留视角、其他模型、参考选择及变换；中英文界面。

## 安装包

发布工作流会自动附加以下文件：

| 文件 | 用途 |
| --- | --- |
| modeldock-0.2.0.vsix | VS Code：扩展菜单 → 从 VSIX 安装；也适用于在 VS Code 中使用 Codex 的工作流 |
| dsh-plugin-modeldock-0.2.0.tgz | DeepSeek Harness 原生文件预览插件 |
| modeldock-openai-0.2.0.zip | 支持文件入口及授权资源读取的 OpenAI Desktop 插件 |
| modeldock-0.2.0-source.zip | 完整源码、预构建运行文件、安装包、许可及匹配的 CAD 依赖源码 |
| SHA256SUMS.txt | 四个归档的 SHA-256 校验值 |

使用说明：[中文 README](https://github.com/Afloat16/modeldock/blob/main/README.zh-CN.md) · [Harness 安装](https://github.com/Afloat16/modeldock/blob/main/adapters/deepseek-harness/README.md) · [OpenAI Desktop 安装](https://github.com/Afloat16/modeldock/blob/main/docs/openai-integration.md)。

## 验证与边界

- 105 项自动测试；共享浏览器 15 组、对比界面 9 组、OpenAI 旧资源路径 7 组、大文件范围路径 6 组，另有真实 stdio 验证。
- 真实安装的 DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-alpha.2 Web 通过 8 组检查，包括超过 5 GiB 的 PLY/STL；真实 VS Code 1.96.4 已在 GitHub CI 中通过四阶段原生验收，包括这两种大文件。
- 大文件用例使用真实稀疏文件，验证大小、偏移、范围读取和渲染，不代表密集 5 GiB 数据的吞吐性能基准。
- 5 GiB 能力是二进制 PLY/STL 的采样预览；大型 PLY 网格当前仅显示采样顶点，面拓扑会明确标为省略。其他格式保持 128 MiB 普通解析边界；不支持完整 5 GiB STEP/IGES/BREP 转换。
- 比较指标描述加载/采样后的几何，最大值不是精确 Hausdorff 距离；单位必须确认，ICP 不自动修正比例，也不保证全局配准。
- OpenAI 使用真实应用和 MCP 服务、模拟 Desktop 宿主进行验证；尚未完成专有 Desktop 软件的实际安装验收。CLI、Work Web 和移动端不声明原生 3D 文件入口能力。
- 发布前依赖扫描为 0 项已知漏洞；这不等于独立安全审计。

详见 [验证记录](https://github.com/Afloat16/modeldock/blob/main/docs/validation.md)。原始项目源码和原创样例采用 MIT；CAD 依赖保留自身 LGPL 许可，匹配源码随完整源码包提供。

最终发布提交：`2f93e45f0b47ee7f842abd9f86ddcc4e79983c4c`。[完整 CI 已通过](https://github.com/Afloat16/modeldock/actions/runs/40856160717)，包含浏览器流程、依赖审计和独立的 VS Code 原生任务。

published_releases.body:
## Email-first human input

Send the complete reviewed steps and an ordinary official login/action link in the email. There is no blanket requirement to return to GPT for every interaction.

- Optional canonical `action`: bounded numbered steps, ordinary reply prompt, and completion hint
- Explicit email-only action opt-in: `AAN_INCLUDE_ACTION=1` or `--include-action` in the producer
- Configured `AAN_SMTP_REPLY_TO`, exact transmitted Message-ID, request reference and current revision
- `aan replies ingest --file message.eml` and `aan replies list` for a durable unverified-input review inbox
- Current-request checks, replay/conflict protection, bounded MIME parsing, and obsolete-note handling
- Additive SQLite v1 → v2 migration, preserving existing event identities, pending requests, and queued deliveries
- Explicit database paths work without a home-directory profile

[English setup](https://github.com/Afloat16/agent-action-notifier/blob/v0.2.0/docs/email-first.md) · [中文设置指南](https://github.com/Afloat16/agent-action-notifier/blob/v0.2.0/docs/email-first.zh-CN.md)

## Important limits

Reply import is local and explicit. This release does not poll a mailbox, authenticate an email author, create an agent-answer channel, or configure SMTP/provider access. Imported replies always remain `pending_unverified` with `can_authorize: false`; they cannot approve, execute, resolve, or resume actions. A separately authorized host must establish owner intent and apply its original confirmation policy. Required platform confirmation forms still use their required surface. Passwords and sign-in credentials stay on the official service.

Defaults remain generic. Review action content before opting in: heuristic redaction cannot guarantee removal of private information. SMTP acceptance does not prove inbox delivery or human attention. No live SMTP/inbox/desktop end-to-end delivery was established.

## Upgrading

Back up your existing SQLite state using a consistent SQLite backup while producers/workers are stopped; do not copy only a live WAL-backed `.db` file. First use of 0.2.0 upgrades the database to schema v2. Version 0.1.0 cannot open that upgraded schema; downgrade requires your retained v1 backup. Nothing installs a background service or creates credentials.

## Downloads

Python 3.10+ is required. The `.pyz` runs without third-party runtime dependencies or package installation. The wheel and source archive are alternatives. Verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

## 中文摘要

新版本可以将经审阅的完整操作步骤和官方登录/操作入口直接写进邮件，并提供普通问题的回复提示，不再要求每次都回到 GPT。需要在生产方明确启用邮件正文，并自行配置 SMTP 和回复邮箱。

本地 `.eml` 导入只生成“未经验证的待处理输入”，不会自动收邮件、确认身份、授权、执行或恢复任务。平台要求的确认表单仍须在指定界面完成；密码与登录凭据留在官方服务。升级会保留旧事件、请求和发送队列并迁移数据库，回退旧版本须使用提前保存的一致性备份。

## Verification

158 unique stdlib tests pass locally. The exact final commit `80a5cd2f881c5e7a62e03cfcf9dac2bb5780266b` passed all nine Linux/macOS/Windows × Python 3.10/3.12/3.14 CI jobs, including compilation and zipapp smoke. SMTP tests are mocked; webhook tests exercise real loopback HTTP. The zipapp, wheel, and source archive were checked byte-for-byte against committed Python source. [CI evidence](https://github.com/Afloat16/agent-action-notifier/actions/runs/37247755439).

# Agent Action Notifier 0.1.0

Durable, notification-only alerts when an agent needs human input, permission, or review.

## Included

- CLI/stdin and authenticated loopback webhook integration
- SQLite pending-request state and transactional at-least-once outbox
- Deduplication, retry/backoff, crash-lease recovery and stale-report handling
- Certificate-verified SMTP; same-session Linux/macOS alerts and Windows notification-area balloons
- Date-checked Codex/Claude hooks plus an explicit host integration contract
- Generic-by-default content, opt-in redacted summaries, safe review links

- `agent_action_notifier-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl`: offline-installable wheel
- `agent-action-notifier-0.1.0-source-8cb5969.zip`: exact reviewed source snapshot
- `SHA256SUMS.txt`: integrity hashes for those three files

Requires Python 3.10+. Run `python agent-action-notifier.pyz demo` for a harmless local example. Read the setup/integration/security guides before selecting real notification channels. SMTP settings must be supplied securely; desktop delivery requires a supported interactive local session.

## Verification and boundaries

111 unique stdlib tests, compilation, standalone demo and offline wheel installation passed locally. The [exact-commit CI run](https://github.com/Afloat16/agent-action-notifier/actions/runs/37177390555) passed all nine Linux/macOS/Windows × Python 3.10/3.12/3.14 jobs. Release target: `8cb5969f9a20a90f4db84f19d6dd3a992630baa6`.

SMTP and desktop/subprocess adapter tests are mocked; webhook tests use actual loopback HTTP. No real mailbox delivery, visible popup, PowerShell notification execution, or live vendor-agent integration was exercised. Transport acceptance is not an inbox/display/read receipt. Windows uses a finite notification-area balloon request, not a native WinRT toast.

This release does not install services, configure credentials, deploy a public endpoint, or automatically attach to ChatGPT. Notifications never authorize, answer or resume an agent action; original human approval and security enforcement remain in charge. Work requiring approval stays paused, while separately authorized independent work can be reported honestly.

# 🛡️ Anti-REA Forge

[English](README.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

![Anti-REA Forge banner](assets/anti-rea-forge.svg)

> **Reduce release exposure. Keep authorization in a trusted service. Contribute in Python or JavaScript.**

Anti-REA Forge is an MIT-licensed toolkit for software release checks and protection research in the era of **REA and AI-assisted reverse engineering**. It combines portable Python release scanning, a JavaScript/TypeScript build interface, CMake integration, C++ sensitive-memory components, PE/ELF gates and request-bound server authorization.

**Bring software protection into your engineering workflow:** catch avoidable release exposure before shipping, give sensitive native data an explicit lifetime, and bind server authorization to the actual request. Explore the examples, integrate a component, or help build the next release.

**MIT · 0.6.0 / Alpha · Python core · JavaScript + TypeScript types · C/C++ integration**

[Portable quick start](docs/portable-release.md) · [Contribute](CONTRIBUTING.en.md) · [贡献指南](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Roadmap (Chinese)](docs/ROADMAP.zh-CN.md) · [Runtime integration](docs/runtime-protection.md)

The tooling retains the **Open Release Guard** Python distribution name `open-release-guard`, CLI/import name `releaseguard`, and existing CMake interfaces. Portable scanning works on release directories without a native entry file; native structural checks target Windows PE and Linux ELF. It is independently developed and is not affiliated with or endorsed by REA.

**New here?** Start with the [community guide and runnable examples](docs/community/README.md), read the [project story](docs/community/PROJECT_STORY.md), or share the [English/Chinese introductions](docs/community/SHARE_COPY.md) with developers interested in software protection. Small contributions are welcome.

## New in v0.6: build-only setup and scoped analysis authorization

Initialize an editable configuration once, then check the completed release after each build:

```bash
python -m pip install -e .
python -m releaseguard project-init --root ./dist --product MyApp
python -m releaseguard check
```

- **No new application runtime integration.** `project-init`, `check` and `prepare` run in the build/release environment. `prepare` scans and signs the same inventory into external sidecars without rewriting the application, its binary signatures or runtime code. Configuration paths are relative to the config file; existing outputs are never overwritten.
- **Deterministic checks before cooperating analysis tools run.** Signed analysis grants bind the exact signed manifest, product/release, authenticated subject, gateway audience, independent `inspect` / `decompile` / `instrument` scopes and a validity period of at most 24 hours. The verifier rechecks the whole release and the clock without caching allow decisions.
- **A direct JavaScript/TypeScript enforcement point.** `withAnalysisAuthorization` calls a fixed handler only after authorization succeeds. Denial, protocol/process failure, expiry or cancellation before admission prevents that call. `checkProject` and `checkAnalysis` expose typed reports for build and gateway integration.
- **Evidence-based AI boundary.** REA explicitly marks target strings and code as untrusted data. The [new source review](docs/rea-agent-authorization-2026-11-05.zh-CN.md) explains why target notices cannot reliably force a third-party model to refuse, and where operator-controlled enforcement can work.

Read the [step-by-step integration guide](docs/analysis-authorization.md), [runnable handler example](examples/javascript/authorized-analysis.mjs) and [v0.6 validation](docs/testing-v0.6-2026-11-05.md). Public notices explain a workflow; they do not override software licenses, prove legal ownership or supply their own trusted public key. Direct REA calls outside the gateway remain outside this control. Build scanning and preflight verification still consume resources; unchanged application bytes are not a universal runtime benchmark.

## v0.5: portable checks and easier contributions

- **Use the same release check from any build system.** `scan-release` inspects the whole staging directory, so Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java and other projects no longer need a PE/ELF entry artifact. Keep using `gate` when native structural checks are needed.
- **Catch avoidable source and key exposure.** Check source-map markers, private-key PEM markers, explicit literals in five encodings, path rules, known file hashes and optional exact file inventories. ZIP-family packages are inspected under byte, entry and nesting limits without extraction; unsupported or incomplete checks cannot produce a passing result.
- **Contribute with Python, JavaScript or TypeScript types.** The [Node.js package](packages/releaseguard/README.md) is plain ESM JavaScript with `.d.ts` declarations, no npm runtime dependencies and no build step. It safely calls the installed Python core; no second cryptographic implementation is introduced. It is a local package, not a published npm release.
- **Ground changes in current REA code.** The [2026-11-04 source review](docs/rea-source-review-2026-11-04.zh-CN.md) pins REA source version 6.8.0, follows source-map, ZIP, Ghidra and Frida paths, and records the limits of each defense.

After creating a Python virtual environment and installing this checkout with `python -m pip install -e .`, scan your completed release directory:

```bash
python -m releaseguard scan-release --root ./dist --policy examples/policy-portable-release.json
```

Exit **0** means configured checks passed, **3** means findings block release, and **2** means the check could not complete. Edit the [portable policy](examples/policy-portable-release.json) for your application. It permits intentionally distributed source code; it is not a universal secret detector. Read the [integration guide](docs/portable-release.md), [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.en.md) and [validation record](docs/testing-v0.5-2026-11-04.md).

These changes reduce accidental disclosure and integration friction. They do not establish resistance to decompilation, a live memory hook or client-side patching. No new end-to-end REA protection result is claimed.

## v0.4: reduce runtime exposure and enforce requests outside the client

- **Native sensitive buffers:** the C++17 `releaseguard::secure_buffer` owns guarded, non-executable pages, checks memory locking, clears its allocation before release, and reports actual protection status. Linux can exclude these pages from core dumps. Windows reports no dump exclusion in this version. None of these measures stop a hook from observing data while it is used.
- **Request-bound server capabilities:** separate-domain Ed25519 signatures bind the authenticated subject, audience, product, operation and exact request bytes, with a maximum lifetime of 300 seconds. A persistent SQLite replay store atomically permits one consumption and rejects trusted-clock rollback. Issuer keys, verification, replay state and the protected operation belong in the trusted service.
- **REA-specific threat mapping:** we inspect REA's pinned 6.7.0 source and its Frida script bridge, and distinguish memory snapshots, live hooks, local branch replacement and replay. The research notes cover formal 2024–2026 security papers and mature secure-memory projects, with explicit limits on what has been implemented.

Read the [runtime integration guide](docs/runtime-protection.md), [中文说明](docs/runtime-protection.zh-CN.md) and [v0.4 validation](docs/testing-v0.4-2026-10-20.md). These components require application integration; the Python cryptographic APIs still return managed `bytes`, and this release does not deploy a hosted authorization service, TLS, authentication or a TEE. Single-use authorization is not exactly-once business execution. A stolen valid bearer capability can still be used first for its original request.

## v0.3: remove recoverable secrets and check the whole release

The supplied REA case study motivates three implemented improvements:

- **One-way password verification:** `password-create` / `password-check` use salted Argon2id with a fixed 64 MiB, 3-pass, 4-lane profile. Untrusted verifier parameters are rejected before expensive work. The original password is not encrypted into the verifier; weak passwords can still be guessed and local checks can be patched.
- **External-key data assets:** `asset-keygen` / `asset-seal` / `asset-open` combine a random external 256-bit master key, per-package HKDF-SHA256 key derivation and AES-256-GCM. Authentication binds trusted product, release, purpose and asset identity. Wrong keys, tampering and context swaps fail before plaintext output is created. Keep the key outside the client release; an authorized process holding its key or plaintext remains observable.
- **Whole-release exposure checks:** `gate --root` can reject source/backup path components, known old artifact SHA-256 digests, missing or additional files against an exact allowlist, and declared literals in every release file, under a byte budget. The [strict native-release policy](examples/policy-strict-release.json) is an editable example, not a universal secret scanner.

These are Python APIs and CLI/build tools. They do not add a native C/C++ verifier/decryptor SDK, executable virtualization, a server or a key service. A fully offline client cannot keep a permanent key secret from someone who controls it. For logic that must remain confidential, keep execution and authorization in a trusted service and expose only the required operation.

See the [English integration and threat mapping](docs/crypto-protection.md), [中文说明](docs/crypto-protection.zh-CN.md), [v0.3 validation](docs/testing-2026-10-20.md), and [functional crypto observations](docs/results/crypto-boundary-2026-10-20.json). The observations include successful recovery of a weak-password control and explicitly record that authorized plaintext is available in memory. They are not a completed REA cracking evaluation or a protection success rate.

## Evidence so far

| Evaluation | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| v0.6 committed cross-platform validation | **All six CI jobs passed**; both Linux Python versions passed 432 tests, JS passed 63 unit/process tests on Linux/macOS and 62 with 1 POSIX skip on Windows, with 9 real bridge integrations on every platform. Windows/MSVC, skip counts and unchanged-target controls are recorded in [validation](docs/testing-v0.6-2026-11-05.md) |
| v0.5 local portable/native integration | **377 Python tests: 376 passed, 1 skipped; 44 JS tests and 5 real CLI integration tests passed**, on 2026-11-04. [Scope, package checks and limits](docs/testing-v0.5-2026-11-04.md) |
| v0.4 local functional/native integration | **331 run: 330 passed, 1 skipped**, on 2026-10-20; the skip is unavailable `/proc/self/smaps` inspection. [Detailed scope and Frida failure](docs/testing-v0.4-2026-10-20.md) |
| Local functional and real CMake integration tests | **176 passed, none skipped**, on 2026-10-15, including Windows timestamp compatibility and PE debug-entry classification regressions; see the [validation record (Chinese)](docs/validation.zh-CN.md) |
| GitHub CI | Linux and Windows/MSVC jobs have passed; see the [run history](https://github.com/Afloat16/anti-rea-forge/actions). These runs are separate from the local test count; Windows DLL ABI compatibility remains untested |
| Selected literal masking, release gates, signed manifests, offline license tools | Implemented within the boundaries described below |
| Independent Ghidra static analysis and independent runtime observation | Both recovered a synthetic sample’s test secret; the unmodified original accepted it. The anti-cracking goal failed |
| REA 6.5.0 integrated analysis | Blocked by the test host environment and not completed; this is **not** evidence of successful protection |

Passing tests or release gates does not measure resistance to cracking. REA’s integrated analysis was blocked by process inspection and temporary-directory limitations; standalone Ghidra successfully analyzed the protected sample. The [test report (Chinese)](docs/testing-2026-10-15.zh-CN.md) separates these outcomes and preserves the evidence. We have no credible “high probability of stopping REA” or general cracking-resistance rate.

## Help build and challenge it

- **Reverse engineering:** analyze project-owned or explicitly authorized samples; share reproducible steps, tool versions, and verifiable observations.
- **C/C++:** improve build integration, compatibility, and protection proposals while checking program output and public interfaces.
- **Python and testing:** strengthen PE/ELF checks, environment diagnostics, and experiments that distinguish recovery, timeout, and environmental failure.
- **Windows:** help validate MSVC, EXE/DLL behavior, and compatibility with callers. Existing CI coverage does not replace Windows DLL ABI or real application testing.
- **First contributions:** start with documentation, minimal reproductions, error messages, or test-environment instructions. Small PRs are welcome.

Use **Issues → New issue** for a bug, experiment, or proposal, or submit a PR. Read the [contribution guide (Chinese)](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [code of conduct (Chinese)](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Use synthetic data in public reports; follow [SECURITY.md (Chinese)](SECURITY.md) for sensitive security issues. Fork, star, or share the project with people who want to test and improve it.

## What is implemented

| Component | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `project-init / check / prepare` | Saved build configuration, portable scan and signed external sidecars without rewriting the release |
| `analysis-grant-issue / analysis-check` | Manifest-bound, scoped and time-limited authorization for a cooperating analysis gateway |
| `withAnalysisAuthorization` | Invoke a fixed JavaScript handler once only after a complete allow decision; no callback on preflight failure |
| `scan-release` / Python `scan_release` | Portable whole-directory disclosure checks and bounded ZIP member inspection without a PE/ELF entry file |
| JavaScript ESM + TypeScript declarations | Read-only build integration using the installed Python core, with isolated invocation, typed APIs, timeouts and bounded output |
| `native-init` + `releaseguard_protect(target POLICY ...)` | Generate CMake/C++ build assets, enable Release optimization and LTO, and fail the build when its artifact violates the policy |
| `RG_TEXT("...")` | Apply reversible compile-time masking to selected C++17 literals; decode into an object with a defined lifetime. Build seeds diversify the static payload |
| `releaseguard::secure_buffer` | Explicitly owned native pages with guards, checked locking, clearing and platform-specific dump status |
| `capability-issue / capability-consume / replay-store-init` | Server-side, short-lived, exact-request authorization with persistent atomic replay rejection |
| `gate` | Scan declared literals in five encodings, inspect debug/symbol metadata, reject forbidden sidecars, and require configured PE structural evidence |
| `gate --root` in v0.3 | Optional exact file allowlist, source/backup path rules, old artifact hash denylist, and bounded whole-release literal scans |
| `password-create / password-check` | Fixed-profile, salted Argon2id one-way verifiers with pre-KDF resource validation |
| `asset-keygen / asset-seal / asset-open` | External-key AES-256-GCM data assets with HKDF-SHA256 and trusted context binding |
| `audit` | Read-only inspection of PE32/PE32+ EXE/DLL files, CLR directories, ASLR/DEP/CFG flags and supporting structures, debug directories, and certificate tables |
| `keygen` | Generate a passphrase-encrypted Ed25519 private key and a distributable public key; refuse to overwrite existing files |
| `manifest-sign / manifest-verify` | Sign a complete release inventory; verify hashes, product, and version; reject missing, modified, or extra files |
| `license-issue / license-verify` | Issue and verify portable offline licenses, including product, subject, validity period, and feature permissions |
| `cmake/ReleaseGuard.cmake` | Integrate MSVC/Windows and GCC or Clang/Linux builds; retain the original MSVC `releaseguard_harden` interface |

Selected C++ literals must be marked with `RG_TEXT`. This version does not provide general code virtualization, automatic rewriting of every string, or a C/C++/.NET license runtime SDK. License checks must be integrated into business entry points or a trusted installation/update process. Build seeds are public diversification values, not secret encryption keys.

IDA, Ghidra, .NET decompilers, and other tools can analyze local programs. A person who controls the execution environment can patch client checks. Publishing this source does not disclose your issuer’s private keys; valid release and license signatures still depend on keeping those keys private, fixing a trusted public key, and preserving a trusted verifier. This project has not undergone an independent security audit.

## Build integration

After installation, include the module in your CMake project and call the function after creating the target:

```cmake
include("/path/to/anti-rea-forge/cmake/ReleaseGuard.cmake")
add_executable(myapp main.cpp)
releaseguard_protect(myapp POLICY "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/policy.json")
```

Use a named object for selected C++ literals. The build hook generates and force-includes the build seed header:

```cpp
#include <releaseguard/literal.hpp>
auto message = RG_TEXT("internal-feature-route-v1");
use(message.c_str()); // message must remain alive while its buffer is used
```

The [native integration guide (Chinese)](docs/native-build.zh-CN.md) covers policy files, generating modules from the installed package, and checking the final release directory. Pure C projects can use build hardening and gates; the literal component requires C++17. Other languages and build systems do not currently have automatic conversion backends.

## Install and inspect

Requires Python 3.10 or later. The Python signing tools support Windows, Linux, and macOS. The native build hook currently supports MSVC/Windows and GCC or Clang/Linux. `audit` inspects Windows PE; `gate` checks PE or ELF according to policy. Run these commands from the project root:

```powershell
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install .
releaseguard --help
releaseguard audit C:\releases\MyApp\MyApp.exe
```

The activation command above is for Windows PowerShell. On Linux/macOS, use `source .venv/bin/activate`. If `releaseguard` is not on PATH, use `python -m releaseguard` in the same virtual environment.

`audit` reports static evidence without executing the inspected file. A certificate table does not establish Authenticode trust. Use Windows trust verification for code signatures, for example `signtool verify /pa /all /v MyApp.exe` after installing the Windows SDK. `policy_passed` means the audit found no warnings. With `--strict`, warnings produce exit code 3 and `ok: false`; tool errors produce exit code 2. The report’s `notes` still apply when the static checks pass.

## 1. Generate keys in the issuer’s environment

**Create a private directory outside both the source repository and the release directory.** Adjust the example paths for your machine:

```powershell
mkdir C:\ReleaseGuardKeys
releaseguard keygen --private C:\ReleaseGuardKeys\issuer-private.pem --public .\issuer-public.pem
```

An interactive terminal prompts for and confirms a passphrase of at least 12 UTF-8 bytes. The private key uses encrypted PKCS#8; POSIX creation permissions are 0600. On Windows, protect the directory with appropriate user ACLs and keep an encrypted backup. **Private keys belong only in the controlled issuer environment; never ship them to clients or publish them.** Do not upload passphrases or real customer licenses. Automation may inject `RELEASEGUARD_PASSPHRASE` from a secret manager; do not put the passphrase in scripts or command-line arguments.

Public keys may be public, but the verifier must **pin a trusted public key or its full SHA-256 fingerprint through a trusted channel**. A license or download must not choose its own trusted key. `--public` must point to a previously trusted configuration. If an attacker can replace it, they can issue a matching set of forged materials with their own key.

## 2. Sign and verify a release manifest

Complete the build, tests, and Authenticode signing before placing all distributable files in a clean release directory. Keep the private key outside that directory. The manifest must also remain outside it to avoid self-reference; public keys and licenses can be kept separately:

```powershell
releaseguard manifest-sign --root .\release\MyApp --private C:\ReleaseGuardKeys\issuer-private.pem --product MyApp --release 1.0.0 --out .\MyApp-1.0.0.manifest.json
releaseguard manifest-verify .\MyApp-1.0.0.manifest.json --root .\release\MyApp --public .\issuer-public.pem --product MyApp --release 1.0.0
```

A valid directory returns `"ok": true`. Modified files, missing DLLs, and additional unlisted files fail verification. Output files are created only at new paths; use a new filename for a new release. The complete directory is checked without an option to ignore extra DLLs. `--release` rejects a manifest with a different expected version; the expected version must itself come from a trusted update policy.

Manifest paths use Unicode NFC. The implementation rejects path traversal, absolute paths, Windows device names/ADS/path aliases, case collisions, symbolic links, and reparse points. Manifest creation also rejects common private-key filenames as an additional mistake-prevention measure; this is not a general secret scanner. Store mutable logs, caches, and user data elsewhere.

Signatures verify data; they do not encrypt code or establish that a file is the newest trusted release. Verification covers the bytes read at check time. Secure installation, loading, and update controls are still needed to handle replacement after verification and rollback.

## 3. Issue and verify offline licenses

```powershell
releaseguard license-issue --private C:\ReleaseGuardKeys\issuer-private.pem --product MyApp --subject customer-001 --days 365 --feature export --out .\customer-001.license.json
releaseguard license-verify .\customer-001.license.json --public .\issuer-public.pem --product MyApp --subject customer-001 --require-feature export
```

Manifests and licenses use separate signing domains and cannot substitute for one another. Production systems may also use separate keys for releases and licenses. License times are checked in UTC, with an exclusive expiry boundary. Licenses are readable signed data and **do not encrypt customer information**. This version permits copying licenses and has no device binding, online revocation, or reliable offline protection against clock rollback.

See [examples/verify_startup.py](examples/verify_startup.py) for Python integration. Native C++/C# applications can implement the [v1 format (Chinese)](docs/format-v1.md) using a maintained cryptographic library; this project does not yet supply a tested native verification SDK. Enforce authorization at actual business entry points and check each feature’s permissions. Keep signing private keys, service credentials, and any secrets that must remain confidential in controlled issuer/server environments. Permanent secrets embedded in offline clients are recoverable targets.

## Hardening and validation

Read the [native integration guide (Chinese)](docs/native-build.zh-CN.md), [Windows/.NET build notes (Chinese)](docs/build-hardening.zh-CN.md), and [security model (Chinese)](SECURITY.md). ASLR, DEP, and CFG mitigate exploitation; they do not prevent decompilation. Preserve PDBs in private symbol storage. Assess Native AOT compatibility per project; native analysis remains possible.

```powershell
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
cmake -S examples -B build -A x64
cmake --build build --config Release
ctest --test-dir build -C Release --output-on-failure
```

The CMake commands above target Windows/MSVC. Linux GCC examples and integration tests are covered in the [contribution guide (Chinese)](CONTRIBUTING.md); set `RELEASEGUARD_CMAKE` if CMake is not on PATH. Local results and GitHub CI are recorded separately. CI has exercised Linux and Windows/MSVC builds, but Windows DLL ABI, real business applications, and Windows reverse-engineering resistance remain outside the completed validation.

On Linux, run `python benchmarks/native_compare.py --out comparison.json` for the project-owned ordinary/protected build comparison. Run `python benchmarks/runtime_boundary.py --out runtime-boundary.json` to reproduce plaintext recovery at a dynamic comparison boundary. For the latter, exit 0 means the experiment completed with successful recovery, so the protection goal failed. It generates and analyzes only its own temporary sample and accepts no external binary input. See the [validation record (Chinese)](docs/validation.zh-CN.md) and [full test report (Chinese)](docs/testing-2026-10-15.zh-CN.md) for evidence and limitations.

## Project and contributions

Started by [Afloat16](https://github.com/Afloat16), licensed under [MIT](LICENSE). Fork and submit a PR, or open an issue with experimental results and design suggestions. The [contribution guide (Chinese)](CONTRIBUTING.md) lists verification expectations and beginner-friendly tasks; the [roadmap (Chinese)](docs/ROADMAP.zh-CN.md) defines proposed work and acceptance criteria.

The tools, methods, and synthetic samples are open source. Your application source, production keys, and server implementation do not need to be published with them.

# Research to Fix

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

**Find similar problems, adapt or combine prior solutions, and verify a local repair.**

Research to Fix is a research and repair workflow that follows the [Agent Skills format](https://agentskills.io/specification). For unfamiliar errors, hard-to-reproduce bugs, training instability, or performance regressions, it guides an agent to investigate whether others have solved a similar problem or found a viable approach, then check that approach against the current project's code, versions, and runtime conditions before applying a fix. Compatible parts of different solutions can be combined, with their contributions, adaptations, and joint validation recorded explicitly.

Concept and workflow design: **[Afloat16](https://github.com/Afloat16)**. Maintainer: **Afloat16**.

## Where to start

- To research and repair a project: install the skill, then use the [example requests](#usage).
- To understand source selection and verification: read the [source playbook](skills/research-to-fix/references/source-playbook.md) and [evidence rules](skills/research-to-fix/references/evidence-rules.md).
- To inspect a small reproducible case first: see the [streaming metrics example](examples/streaming-metrics/README.md).
- To reuse a previous repair: [record a case and recall related cases](#record-and-reuse-a-case) from a directory you choose.
- To record multiple research rounds or hand off evidence: use the [helper tools](#helper-tools) and [case template](skills/research-to-fix/references/case-template.md).

## What it does

| Stage | Output |
| --- | --- |
| Problem fingerprint | Redacted error, environment and versions, call path, minimal reproduction, and success criteria |
| Local case reuse | Related recorded solutions, matching terms, version facts, source references, and limitations to recheck |
| Research across sources | Verifiable evidence from GitHub, Hugging Face, Zhihu, Xiaohongshu, original papers, researchers, and labs |
| Applicability analysis | Source conditions mapped to local files and symbols, candidate approaches, compatible components, tradeoffs, and falsifiable hypotheses |
| Repair and experiments | Small code changes, before/after checks of the original symptom, relevant regressions, costs, and limitations |
| Reviewable delivery | Original links, actual commands, exit codes, observations, and a solved / partial / blocked status |

Choose sources by relevance. When full coverage is requested, search each category and explain any unavailable sources. Zhihu and Xiaohongshu can help uncover experience and terminology; technical conclusions still require original materials or local experiments. Famous authors, conference labels, stars, and likes do not replace evidence.

## Installation

Use a host that supports `SKILL.md`. The host provides search and browsing tools; this project does not bundle a search service, login credentials, or a crawler. The helper script requires Python 3.10+.

Install in a supported host after checking the installation tool you use:

```bash
npx skills add Afloat16/research-to-fix --skill research-to-fix
```

Alternatively, clone the repository and copy the complete `skills/research-to-fix` directory into your host's skills directory. Automatic triggering, Python execution, and UI metadata support depend on the host's configuration.

## Usage

```text
Use $research-to-fix: this project occasionally hangs during multi-GPU training.
First reproduce it and record the versions, then research similar issues and
fix PRs online. Adapt or combine compatible solutions, explain the differences
from the current call path, and validate the complete repair.
```

```text
Use $research-to-fix: our reproduction of a paper performs far below its
reported results. Research the authors' code, Hugging Face configuration,
the published paper, and community reproductions. Identify viable approaches
and compare them with the same data splits, seeds, and resource budget.
```

```text
Use $research-to-fix: cover GitHub, Hugging Face, Zhihu, Xiaohongshu,
relevant leading journals and conferences, researchers, and labs.
Record any sources you cannot access truthfully.
```

## Record and reuse a case

From the repository root, generate a case from actual local test runs, check it, then recall it for a related problem:

```bash
python examples/streaming-metrics/record_case.py \
  --output /tmp/research-to-fix-example

python skills/research-to-fix/scripts/research_case.py validate \
  /tmp/research-to-fix-example/case.json --format json

python skills/research-to-fix/scripts/research_case.py recall \
  --cases-dir /tmp/research-to-fix-example \
  --error 'single-use iterator count mean' --limit 3 --format markdown
```

Choose a **new output directory**; `/tmp/research-to-fix-example` is an example location. The separate `record_case.py` example runs the documented broken implementation and the current fixed implementation in an isolated temporary directory, using the same tests and command. It writes `case.json` and the actual logs and per-test outcomes under `runs/`. This example executes its fixed local tests; the main helper never executes commands from a case file.

For your own cases, point `recall` at their directory. It reads only that directory's top-level JSON files and considers only structurally valid records declaring `solved`. The case directory itself and its JSON entries cannot be symbolic links; ancestors in the explicitly supplied path resolve normally. It returns bounded summaries and matching reasons rather than complete command logs. Ranking uses local BM25 keyword matching, including Chinese character pairs; it requires no network, model, embedding service, or additional package. No matching terms means no result, and weak matches are not added merely to fill the limit.

| Recall option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--cases-dir DIR`, `--error TEXT` | Explicit case directory and a local problem description for keyword matching. |
| `--component TEXT` | Optional trimmed, case-insensitive exact component filter. |
| `--version TEXT` | Report a literal `same` / `different` / `unknown` comparison; it does not change ranking or establish compatibility. |
| `--limit N` | Return at most N candidates; default 5, maximum 20. |
| `--format json` / `--format markdown` | Machine-readable output or a readable candidate list. |

Recall results are leads for a new repair. Recheck the current code, conditions, original evidence, and tests before adapting a prior solution. A relevance score is not proof of correctness, and a recorded `solved` status is not independently authenticated. Recall does not automatically redact local content; review excerpts before sharing them. See [case reuse](skills/research-to-fix/references/case-reuse.md) for resource limits, selection rules, and the upstream implementations that informed this design.

## Helper tools

```bash
python skills/research-to-fix/scripts/research_case.py queries \
  --error 'RuntimeError: dtype mismatch' --component pytorch \
  --version 2.5 --concept 'mixed precision' \
  --source github_issues --source huggingface_forum \
  --repo pytorch/pytorch --language en --limit 4

python skills/research-to-fix/scripts/research_case.py init \
  --output /tmp/research-case.json

python skills/research-to-fix/scripts/research_case.py validate \
  /tmp/research-case.json --format json
```

`queries` generates an offline plan. With no source or language filters or limit, it keeps the default 26 English and Chinese candidates; select 4–8 by relevance before searching. Searches for papers, researchers, and labs use mechanism keywords.

| Query option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--source` | Select source categories; repeat to include several. |
| `--language en` / `--language zh` | Select query languages; repeat to include both. |
| `--limit N` | Cap the number of generated candidates with a positive integer. This does not set or execute an online search budget. |
| `--repo owner/name` | Scope GitHub issue and pull-request candidates to one repository; other sources remain unchanged. |

Review every query before sending it. Input checks reject common credential patterns, detected private addresses, and recognized non-HTTP(S) URI forms, but secret detection is heuristic and cannot guarantee safe disclosure.

`init` does not overwrite existing files. `validate` checks record structure and declared references; `--format json` provides machine-readable results. Its exit codes are **0** for a structurally valid record, **1** for record errors, and **2** for file or JSON input errors. The standard-library helper does not access the network, authenticate to services, upload code, or execute recorded commands. Passing validation establishes neither the truth of the record nor a repair's effectiveness or cause.

Schema version remains **1**. Comparison context, repair attempt, adopted solution, and per-test result fields are optional, and the existing single-attempt format remains usable without them. Stricter checks intentionally reject incomplete or inconsistent records, including missing regression after checks, completed searches without dates, and malformed criteria.

A solved record needs an after pass for **every recorded before check**, including regressions, plus at least one failure-to-pass comparison for the original symptom. Matching checks keep their command, criteria, expected exit code, and any declared comparison context consistent. Multiple attempts retain historical failures and explicitly identify the final attempt; a combined solution needs a supporting experiment that covers the whole combination. The [case template](skills/research-to-fix/references/case-template.md) describes these rules and optional fields. An empty blocked template remains valid, and local inference needs no invented external sources.

For test suites, record optional `test_results` with stable test IDs and outcomes. A pass cannot contain zero passing tests, failures, errors, or unexecuted tests. When details are supplied for a before/after comparison, final results must retain every baseline test ID and pass every test that previously passed, failed, or errored; previously skipped tests may remain skipped. Legacy records without these details remain supported, but the validator cannot detect deleted or skipped tests inside their suite from an aggregate exit code alone.

## Project structure

- `skills/research-to-fix/SKILL.md`: core instructions.
- `skills/research-to-fix/references/`: source selection, case reuse, evidence rules, repair workflow, and case template.
- `skills/research-to-fix/scripts/research_case.py`: query planning, local case recall, and record validation.
- `tests/`: behavior checks for the helper tool.
- `examples/`: small independently reproducible cases and practice inputs.

## Validation and contributions

```bash
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python -m unittest discover -s examples/streaming-metrics -v
```

CI runs these checks on Python 3.10 and 3.13, then records, validates, and retrieves the streaming example. Successful jobs retain the case, source snapshots, raw test logs, per-test reports, and retrieval result as `repair-case-python-<version>` artifacts for 7 days. These are reviewable results for this small example, not a general repair-success benchmark.

Contributions based on real problems are welcome. Include the triggering request, environment, redacted reproduction, actual research and local validation, and where the workflow wasted searches or misjudged applicability. Do not upload private code, secrets, or customer data. New sources should explain how to verify original content and record access failures; new scripts should include actual execution results.

The independently tried [streaming metrics case](examples/streaming-metrics/README.md) includes original evidence, a failing baseline, a compatible fix, and reproducible checks. It is a small synthetic case and does not establish effectiveness on large engineering or research problems. The current version cannot guarantee access to every platform, an external answer for every problem, or success for every repair. Record access restrictions and validation gaps.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE).

## Related projects

Browse the [Afloat16 project guide](https://github.com/Afloat16/research-to-fix/blob/main/docs/PROJECTS.md) by task: requirements debate, research and repair, task checks, endpoint diagnostics, notifications, MCP advice, robotics troubleshooting, and 3D reconstruction.

Six domain-specific tools were added in this round. See the [review of 29 threads and 336 comments](docs/DEMAND_REVIEW.md) for their selection and boundaries, and the [outreach record](docs/OUTREACH.md) for actual directory submissions and replies to relevant issues.

# Demand research and tool selection — 2026-10-14

[English](DEMAND_REVIEW.md) | [简体中文](DEMAND_REVIEW.zh-CN.md)

This review selected six specific engineering needs across robotics, LLM tool calling, and 3D reconstruction. Deliverables were limited to diagnostics or format conversions that can be checked locally. The goal is to add evidence to existing ROS, model-service, execution-framework, and reconstruction-engine workflows, helping users clarify problems with inputs, timing, call identity, and coordinate conventions before reporting an issue, comparing versions, or connecting a downstream workflow.

The collected material covers 29 public issue threads and 336 comments, of which 332 were not marked by the platform as comments from bot accounts. At collection time, 16 threads were open and 13 were closed. This is a **purposive sample** selected for relevance to the problems, not a representative survey or a statistical ranking of demand across these fields. More comments do not mean more independent users, a more severe problem, or stronger willingness to pay; repeated follow-ups, disagreements, and troubleshooting by the same person can all increase the count. Project stars are only a dated indicator of reach, not evidence of demand, correctness, or tool quality.

All six projects are currently experimental tools. Public threads establish that a problem was raised; tool documentation states what the current implementation promises. Reproducible inputs and validation results are still needed to connect the two. The links below retain the original discussion entry points without reproducing comment bodies, and these tools are not presented as having resolved the corresponding upstream issues.

| Field | Tool | Scope of this delivery |
|---|---|---|
| Robotics | [bag-timeline-audit](https://github.com/Afloat16/bag-timeline-audit) | Read-only checks for backward time jumps, duplicate timestamps, gaps, and cross-topic pairing on a shared clock in ROS 2 SQLite, MCAP, or JSONL records. |
| Robotics | [tf-route-audit](https://github.com/Afloat16/tf-route-audit) | Checks topology, required frames, conflicts, and observed dynamic time ranges in exported TF records or native URDF. |
| LLM workflows | [sse-toolcall-audit](https://github.com/Afloat16/sse-toolcall-audit) | Checks tool-call assembly, completion state, and argument semantics in saved Chat Completions / Responses SSE; can compare a saved non-streaming response. |
| LLM workflows | [tooltrace-audit](https://github.com/Afloat16/tooltrace-audit) | Checks repeated attempts, overlapping retries, missing results, and call-identity conflicts in explicit execution events or conversation records. |
| 3D reconstruction | [colmap-model-audit](https://github.com/Afloat16/colmap-model-audit) | Read-only checks of fields, bidirectional tracks, consistency, view connectivity, and same-name image overlap in traditional COLMAP text sparse models. |
| 3D reconstruction | [pose-convention-bridge](https://github.com/Afloat16/pose-convention-bridge) | Converts rigid camera poses and related file formats after the user explicitly declares pose direction, camera axes, and the world transform. |

## Selection method and interpretation of evidence

Selection considered recurrence of symptoms across threads, recent follow-ups, effects on data or workflows, the feasibility of offline review, and whether an existing runtime could be reused rather than reimplemented. No weighted score was assigned from comment counts or stars, and the six needs were not ranked as “most urgent.” Selecting two needs per field was an implementation-scope decision, not a claim that demand is equal across the three fields.

- **Original sources remain traceable.** [thread-index.json](thread-index.json) retains thread URLs, status at collection, update dates, comment counts, and comment links. Its 29 threads and 336 comment links allow the review scope to be checked; it contains no comment bodies.
- **Status is not an outcome.** An open thread may already have a workaround. A closed thread may reflect a fix, a duplicate, a version change, or another reason for closure. Closed threads supply historical symptoms and regression leads here, not evidence of a fault that still exists.
- **An update date is not urgency.** Recent replies can help identify conditions still being discussed, but may only add information. Similar behavior across different versions, models, hardware, data, and configurations cannot automatically be assigned the same root cause.
- **The report separates three levels of conclusion.** Symptoms reported in threads, judgments about tool opportunities, and current implementation capabilities are described separately. Passing structural or timing checks does not establish that sensors dropped no frames, execution occurred exactly once, a protocol is fully compatible, or reconstruction accuracy is acceptable.
- **Existing alternatives remain the first option.** If an official tool already performs the actual task, use it first. This comparison explains where a small tool can add diagnostics for a particular input or workflow step; it does not establish that no comparable tools exist.

## Why these six needs entered the implementation scope

| Tool | Demand signals in the sources | Selection rationale and what remains unverified |
|---|---|---|
| bag-timeline-audit | rosbag2 #1845 concerns troubleshooting missing frames during recording; #2173 and #2023 provide historical leads about ordering at identical timestamps and simulation-clock differences. | Separating gaps in recorded data, backward time jumps, and different time bases helps users provide reviewable issue evidence. The tool can inspect only the records it sees; it cannot determine whether a missing record originated at the sensor, transport, recording, or playback stage. Real split bags and complex compressed recordings remain outside the promised scope. |
| tf-route-audit | geometry2 #749, #798, and rosbag2 #2094 concern paths, authority, and old-time data, respectively. | Topology errors and insufficient time coverage can first be isolated offline without installing or running the full ROS stack. Multiple parents in an aggregated export are a finding to review. An edge observed within a time range does not establish continuous queryability, and exported records cannot recover live authority or tf2 cache behavior. |
| sse-toolcall-audit | vLLM #31501, #45449, #39426, and #44676 concern streamed arguments, function names, Responses assembly, and interference from reasoning markers. | Saved service output becomes a repeatably checkable sample for comparing parser or client changes. A capture shows only the visible result received by the client; it cannot by itself assign fault to the model, parser, or network. Differences between two stochastic generations do not automatically establish a regression. |
| tooltrace-audit | LangGraph #7417 raises re-execution of long calls; #8204 concerns call-termination conditions; #8102 discusses pre-execution policy hooks. | Call identity, attempts, and result pairing are shared prerequisites for checking retries and execution records. Offline auditing does not implement the policy interception, scheduling fixes, or idempotency protection discussed in those threads. Callers still need stable IDs, applicable clocks, and complete events to distinguish legitimate retries from duplicate side effects. |
| colmap-model-audit | COLMAP #1703 concerns model merging; #4557 and #4376 provide leads involving versions and multi-camera rigs. | Checking references, tracks, and overlap candidates in traditional text models before merging or downstream use reduces format-level uncertainty. This implementation does not check new rig/frame files or perform multi-camera geometric optimization. Passing structural checks or finding name overlap does not establish that COLMAP/GLOMAP accuracy problems have been resolved. |
| pose-convention-bridge | Nerfstudio #2182, #3101, #3690, and #3484 concern pose integration from ORB-SLAM, RTAB-Map, COLMAP, and dataparser output. | Explicit w2c/c2w direction, camera axes, quaternion order, and world mapping make reversible conversions easier to review. The tool does not infer source extrinsics, world orientation, or scale. Correct matrix conversion still requires actual image correspondence, intrinsics, and scene points to use the same world mapping. |

## Existing tools, competition, and capability boundaries

These alternatives relate directly to the specific workflows reviewed here; this is not a complete competitive landscape. The value of a new project should be established through input compatibility, review effort, and useful reports. Listing a few upstream issues is not enough to claim a gap in existing tooling.

| Tool in this delivery | What existing tools provide | What this tool adds and cannot replace |
|---|---|---|
| bag-timeline-audit | `ros2 bag info/play` provides bag information and playback; [Foxglove](https://docs.foxglove.dev/docs/visualization/connecting/local-data) already supports ROS 2 `.db3`, `.mcap`, and multi-file sources of the same format. | Adds bounded, machine-readable timing checks for a single native file or JSONL without decoding payloads, replaying, or modifying bags. It cannot prove transport loss and does not automatically infer split-file ordering or support compressed SQLite or ROS 1 bags. Cross-topic pairing requires the user to confirm a shared clock; nearest-sample pairing is not certification of sensor synchronization quality. |
| tf-route-audit | [tf2 CLI tools](https://github.com/ros2/geometry2/blob/rolling/tf2_ros/doc/cli_tools.rst) already provide live diagnostics for frame graphs, timing statistics, chains, and broadcasters. | Adds checks of explicit exported records and native URDF without ROS. It does not implement tf2 caching, interpolation, transform composition, or live authority discovery, and it does not parse xacro. An observed dynamic range containing a timestamp does not guarantee queryability at that timestamp; movable URDF joints provide no evidence of runtime pose timing. |
| sse-toolcall-audit | vLLM parsers are server-side implementations; [LLM Handshake](https://github.com/Afloat16/llm-handshake) performs explicitly authorized live Chat Completions probes and does not test Responses. | Reads saved raw Chat Completions / Responses SSE offline, assembles calls, and checks completion markers, strict object arguments, and semantic comparisons. It is not a conformance test for every protocol field. It executes no tools, makes no network requests, does not fix vLLM, and cannot classify differences between two stochastic generations as a definite fault. |
| tooltrace-audit | [LangGraph persistence](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/persistence) supports resumption through checkpoints; [LangSmith](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/observability) provides tracing and observability. [Side effects during resumption](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/interrupts) still require appropriate idempotency design; tracing alone does not guarantee exactly-once execution. | Checks a documented event contract and also provides an explicitly enabled Recorder; it does not claim direct import of native LangGraph/LangSmith archives. Execution mode requires stable identity and comparable clocks within the same run; conversation mode can check only call/result ordering. Repeated argument signatures are review candidates, not proof of duplicate execution or an infinite loop. It does not intercept, cancel, or deduplicate tools, or fix checkpoint scheduling. |
| colmap-model-audit | The [COLMAP CLI](https://colmap.github.io/cli.html) already provides `model_converter` and `model_analyzer`; [PyCOLMAP](https://colmap.github.io/pycolmap/pycolmap.html) already checks internal consistency and finds commonly registered images. The [official model format](https://colmap.github.io/format.html) also includes rigs/frames. | The differences are a standard-library implementation, traditional text triples, explicit checks, and bounded JSON reports; consistency and overlap checks are not claimed as new capabilities. Binary models require official conversion first. Residuals are computed only for PINHOLE / SIMPLE_PINHOLE; unknown or new camera models are explicitly unverified. Shared names identify merge candidates, not geometric registration, database compatibility, or rig calibration. The tool does not reconstruct, merge, filter, or repair upstream software. |
| pose-convention-bridge | [Nerfstudio coordinate conventions](https://docs.nerf.studio/quickstart/data_conventions.html) and its [dataparser](https://docs.nerf.studio/_modules/nerfstudio/data/dataparsers/base_dataparser.html) already define training inputs, parser transforms, and inverse mappings. | Adds explicit, verifiable rigid pose-direction and camera-axis conversions, plus a declared world mapping; it is not a complete parser or calibration workflow. `--dataparser-transform` uses the declared forward mapping and does not automatically invert it or compose `applied_transform`. It does not infer the up axis, centering, scale, or RTAB-Map extrinsics. Intrinsics/distortion are passed through, not calibrated or undistorted; scene points/meshes must separately receive the same world mapping. |

## How to judge whether these deliverables are useful

Current documentation positions the tools as experimental implementations, with synthetic inputs used in examples and tests. Configuring cross-platform CI is not equivalent to validation on real robot bags, complete server stacks, production execution frameworks, or large reconstruction scenes. Actual CI outcomes must come from the corresponding Actions records. Passing structural checks is also no substitute for acceptance of the actual workflow.

Next validation should use authorized local samples with explicit expectations: timing audits should distinguish record gaps from mixed clocks; TF checks should distinguish missing paths from insufficient temporal evidence; SSE checks should include parallel calls, missing fields, and truncation; execution traces should cover both legitimate retries and repeated attempts; COLMAP checks should compare independently constructed broken references with valid models; pose conversions should use known camera centers, directions, and non-unit world scales to check round trips and mapping order. Only these validation results can support the corresponding capability claims. Discussion counts cannot establish adoption, diagnostic benefit, or performance gains.

Input files and exported reports can still contain sensitive metadata such as image names, topic/frame names, call IDs, times, and hashes. Local execution or omission of some report content does not imply anonymization. Data owners must review material before sharing; do not upload real captures, user attachments, private data, or credentials without permission.
